annotations.text: Both/And — Memphis Geometric Pop, full screen set (row 1: daily loop, row 2: nav-accessible)
Expert (3-circle) variants — players fill all 4 overlap regions (3 pairwise + center)
Visual style directions — all showing the Today's Puzzle screen

A — Editorial Minimal: NYT Games-style restraint. Reads as a ‘smart puzzle,’ calm and confident.

Tradeoff: lower visual energy — could feel dry to more casual players.

B — Bold Pop Playful: high-energy, broad mobile-game appeal, very shareable.

Tradeoff: leans more mass-casual than ‘clever wordplay niche.’

C — Retro Paper/Handcrafted: cute and crafted — matches ‘Both/And’ as a clever, personal name.

Tradeoff: hand-drawn wobble effects add a bit more visual complexity to keep consistent across every screen.

D — Dark Neon Arcade: tech/night-owl energy, glowing circles, terminal-style prompts.

Tradeoff: dark UI needs careful contrast tuning for long reading sessions, and the pixel font is only legible at small doses.

E — Soft Pastel Zen: calm, breathable, wellness-app energy — wordplay as a gentle daily ritual.

Tradeoff: lower contrast and softness could read as less ‘game-like’ or make the CTA less obvious at a glance.

F — Memphis Geometric Pop: loud, graphic, 90s-postmodern — confetti shapes, tilted layout, poster energy. CHOSEN — built out into the full screen set on the Screens page.

Tradeoff: busiest of all six directions; the decorative shapes need care so they never crowd real content or hurt legibility.
Earlier fork: how should Expert voting work? Decision: players fill all 4 regions (option B) — built out as TodayExpert / FillInExpert / VoteExpert / ResultsExpert on the Screens page.

A (not chosen) — users only fill the center blank; the 3 pairwise overlaps come pre-filled by the app. Kept the Vote screen unchanged from Novice, but required a much heavier content pipeline (6 pre-filled items/day instead of 3).
B (chosen) — users fill all 4 overlap regions; each submission is the full solved diagram. Voting became one-submission-at-a-time instead of a scrollable list.
